Central bank holds rates steady

By Jane Example, Business Reporter

The central bank of Examplia left its main interest rate unchanged on Thursday, saying inflation was easing more slowly than policymakers had hoped and that the labour market remained resilient despite weaker hiring in the construction sector.

Governor Alex Sample told reporters that the decision was unanimous. "We want to be sure that price growth is firmly on the way to our target before we start lowering borrowing costs," he said, adding that the bank would publish fresh forecasts next month.

Economists had widely expected the pause. Markets nevertheless moved after the statement, with the national currency firming against the dollar and government bond yields slipping by a few basis points as traders trimmed bets on an early cut.

Households have been squeezed by high mortgage payments for most of the year. Lenders said on Wednesday that new loan approvals fell for the third month in a row, while the average rate on a two-year fixed deal edged down only slightly from last month's peak.

Analysts at several banks said the first reduction is now more likely in the spring than in the winter. "Patience is the message," said one strategist. "The bank does not want to repeat the mistake of easing too soon and having to reverse course."

The next policy meeting is scheduled for the middle of next month, when the bank will also publish its quarterly report on financial stability and its updated view of the housing market.
